songInfo.title: Have You Ever Seen the Rain

scalesUsed.notes: C - D - E - F - G - A - B - C
scalesUsed.application: Provides the entire diatonic foundation for the verse and chorus chords (C, G, Am, F)
Forms the sweet, soulful vocal melody line sung by John Fogerty

keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Ionian (Major) with driving, soulful Americana acoustic warmth
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: A minor is the relative minor of C major

mainProgression.description: The quintessential pop and classic rock progression in C major. John Fogerty elevates the classic formula by inserting an unforgettable stepwise bass walkdown (C - C/B - Am - Am/G) in the chorus.

sectionProgressions.description: The verse alternates between tonic C and dominant G with a steady, driving down-up rhythm pulse

sectionProgressions.progression: F - G - C - C/B - Am - Am/G - F - G - C
sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: IV - V - I - I/VII - vi - vi/V - IV - V - I
sectionProgressions.description: The signature chorus starts with a powerful lift to IV (F), then moves through V (G) into the legendary descending bass walkdown through C, C/B, Am, and Am/G
Acoustic strumming establishing the tempo and introducing the dynamic contrast between minor and major chords
Open position C major scale study developing finger independence and clean string articulation

harmonicFunction: C (I) - Tonic chord giving the song its bright, steady, comforting foundation
G (V) - Dominant chord creating tension that resolves cleanly back to C
Am (vi) - Relative minor introducing introspective emotional depth in the chorus
F (IV) - Subdominant chord providing the soaring melodic lift on the word 'rain'

techniques.name: Descending Stepwise Bass Walkdown
techniques.description: Walking single bass notes down along the 5th and 6th strings between chord changes (C at 3rd fret, B at 2nd fret, open A, then low G on 6th string 3rd fret)

notes: C/B transition: Lift your ring finger, place middle/index on 5th string (2nd fret)
Am/G transition: Hit 6th string (3rd fret) while holding the Am shape
sequence: Hold full C major chord and strum for 2 beats
Play the single B note on the 5th string 2nd fret on beat 3
Switch cleanly to open Am on beat 4
Fret the low G note on string 6 to complete the descent into F
tips: Do not rush the B transition note — it acts as a passing bridge into Am
Keep the top strings quiet or lightly muted during the single bass notes
Practice the walkdown slowly at 70 BPM before bringing it to the 116 BPM recording speed

techniques.name: Driving Acoustic Rhythm Strum
techniques.description: Steady, relaxed 8th-note strumming with accented downstrokes on beats 2 and 4 that captures John Fogerty's infectious CCR bounce

notes: Keep right wrist loose and pivoting from the joint
Emphasize the bottom bass strings on beat 1 and full strums on 2 and 4
sequence: Beat 1: Downstroke emphasizing lower bass strings
Beat 2: Downstroke with accent across all strings
Beat & : Upstroke brushing top treble strings
Beat & (after 3): Upstroke catching the treble strings on the offbeat
Beat 4: Downstroke, followed by quick upstroke on the &
tips: Maintain continuous hand movement even when you do not hit the strings (ghost strumming)
Relax your grip on the pick so it glides smoothly across the strings
Listen to Fogerty's percussive right hand for dynamic cues

sections.name: Intro
sections.description: The song opens with an iconic acoustic rhythm chop setting up the steady 116 BPM groove before Fogerty's vocals enter.
notes: Count in at 116 BPM with relaxed confidence
Clear distinction between the warm Am and bright C
Lock in with the drum beat on 2 and 4

sections.name: Verse
sections.description: The verse glides effortlessly between C and G, giving the lyrics space to resonate before the chorus arrives.
notes: Keep the strumming hand moving in unbroken eighth notes
Clean transitions between the open C and open G shapes

sections.name: Chorus (with Bass Walkdown)
sections.description: The high point of the song: soaring vocals on F, leading into the beloved C - C/B - Am - Am/G descending bass line.
sections.progression: F - G - C - C/B - Am - Am/G - F - G - C
notes: Deliver the F chord with full energy
Execute the bass note walk: C (3rd fret 5th string) to B (2nd fret) to open A string
Resolve cleanly back through F and G into C

sections.name: Scale Practice Exercise
sections.description: Two-octave open C major scale exercise showing the exact diatonic note pool utilized across the song.
notes: Use alternate picking across all 5 strings
Emphasize the root C notes (5th string 3rd fret and 2nd string 1st fret)
Strive for crisp string separation without extraneous buzzing
sections.exerciseLabel: Open C Major Diatonic Scale Run

guitar.recommended: Dreadnought or 000 Acoustic Guitar (Martin D-18, Gibson J-45)
alternatives: Fender Stratocaster or Telecaster on neck pickup
guitar.pickup: Under-saddle transducer or condenser microphone placed 12 inches from 12th fret

amp.recommended: Fender Twin Reverb or clean acoustic combo

effects.reverb: Subtle vintage spring reverb for warmth
effects.other: Thin-to-medium pick (0.50mm to 0.73mm) for flexible acoustic strumming

beginner.title: Master the Core Open Chords (C, G, Am, F)
steps: Learn the open C, G, and Am chord shapes cleanly
Practice an easier F major shape (Fmaj7: X-X-3-2-1-0 or F/C: X-3-3-2-1-X) if full barre F is challenging
Work on switching back and forth between C and G without stopping
Strum steady quarter notes along with the recording

intermediate.title: Master the Descending Bass Walkdown
steps: Isolate the C - C/B - Am - Am/G bass walkdown with a metronome at 75 BPM
Target the specific bass strings while keeping your rhythm hand steady
Build tempo gradually to the full 116 BPM recording speed
Smoothly integrate the full barre F chord into the chorus progression

advanced.title: Full Campfire Performance with Dynamics & Vocals
steps: Add subtle percussive chucks on beats 2 and 4 to emulate the drum snare
Sing lead vocals while navigating the descending bass walkdown
Incorporate light hammer-on fills on the open C chord (D string 2nd fret)
Perform the entire song seamlessly from memory

commonMistakes: Stumbling on the F chord in the chorus — use an open Fmaj7 as a stepping stone if needed
Rushing the B passing bass note during the walkdown
Strumming too aggressively and drowning out the walking bass notes
Losing the relaxed 116 BPM bounce by playing with a stiff right arm
practiceRoutine: 2 minutes: Warm up with C, G, Am, and F chord changes
5 minutes: Isolated practice of the C → C/B → Am → Am/G walkdown with a metronome
5 minutes: Verse groove (C - G - C) at 116 BPM with down-up strumming
5 minutes: Full chorus run-through connecting the F chord into the walkdown
5 minutes: Complete song play-through focusing on vocal cues and steady dynamics
focusAreas: Clean bass string targeting on the descending walkdown
Effortless transitions to the F chord
Steady right-hand rhythm motion at 116 BPM
Relaxed campfire acoustic tone and feel
metronomeWork: Set metronome to 80 BPM and drill the 4-measure chorus walkdown
Increase by 6 BPM increments until you reach 116 BPM
Practice with clicks only on beats 2 and 4 for authentic roots-rock groove
Verify you don't slow down during the F chord transition
